title: `min`, `max` and `max_horizontal` skip NaN
verdict: NaN is ignored unless every value is NaN; `nan_max` propagates it
description: `max` over 1, NaN, -inf, inf is inf and `arg_max` points at inf, though `sort` puts NaN last: the aggregates skip NaN, and give NaN only when there is nothing else (`max(NaN, NULL)` is NaN). `pl.max_horizontal(x, NaN)` is x. `nan_max` and `nan_min` propagate NaN.
`min` and `min_horizontal` agree with NaN-as-greatest, since a NaN is never the least of a group with a number.
`Float32` and `Float64` share the code, and the streaming reducers call the in-memory kernel per morsel and merge with the same `min_ignore_nan`, so both widths and both engines skip NaN.
The `nan_min` docstring names numpy's `nanmax` and gets numpy's NaN handling backwards: PL-10, a text fix.
No upstream test pins NaN in `min` and `max` on the streaming engine; it may change between versions.
reference: `MAX`, `greatest` follow `nan_order: GREATEST`, so `max(1, NaN)` is NaN. The writer needs `nan_max` (or a sort) for `max` of doubles and a NaN check for `greatest`; 20 of 144 rows of `greatest` differ.

provenance.notes: `sverify_dev.probe_polars` runs each expression on edge cases (0, ±1, ±2, 3, ±7, the bounds of the integer width; 0.5, ±2.5, 7, 1e308, ±inf, NaN; NULL), one row at a time, and compares each row with Lean's outcome of the Substrait call under each candidate option (`substrait-check --outcomes`). Observations are Polars programs whose result is recorded as it is. Polars 2.1.0 (Python), Rust crates at tag py-2.1.0 (commit 7f902bd3), on macOS arm64.

evidence.note: floats: `min_ignore_nan` is `f32::min`/`f64::min`, `max_ignore_nan` `max`; one macro for `f32` and `f64`
SIMD kernel: `simd_min`/`simd_max` from a NaN start, then `reduce_min`/`reduce_max`
the kernel for `f32` (16 lanes) and `f64` (8 lanes)
`ChunkAgg::min`/`max`: the sorted flag's first or last value, else the kernel per chunk merged by `min_ignore_nan`
ungrouped streaming reduce: each pipeline folds its morsels into a local state (`update_group`), the local states merge in pipeline order (`combine_subset`)
`VecGroupedReduction`: `update_group` calls `reduce_ca` on a morsel; `update_groups_subset` calls `reduce_one` per row
Float32 and Float64 column [1.0, NaN, -1.0] in one group: min -1.0 and max 1.0, in select and group_by, in memory and streaming

provenance.notes: Polars 2.1.0 (Python) from the project's environment, macOS arm64, `POLARS_MAX_THREADS=2`; each `LazyFrame` collected with `engine="in-memory"` and `engine="streaming"`.

evidence.note: Example: [-1.0, NaN, 1.0].max() is 1.0 (SRC py-polars/src/polars/expr/expr.py L3609-L3627); min gives -1.0 (L3666-L3684).
nan_max/nan_min 'propagate/poison encountered NaN values'; Polars 'defaults to ignoring them' (expr.py L3723-L3769).

`test_nan_in_group_by_agg`, `test_nan_aggregations`, `test_sorted_nan_max_12931`: max/min skip NaN ([1, NaN, 2, 3] max 3.0 min 1.0, nan_max/nan_min NaN; sorted [1, 2, NaN] max 2.0), select and group_by, eager, in memory.
`test_nan_inf_aggregation`: group [NaN, 5] min 5 max 5, [NaN, None] NaN, eager.
`test_min_max_horizontal_with_nan_28682`: min_horizontal(NaN, 20, 30) 20, max_horizontal 30, eager. No streaming test with NaN in min/max.
